messages:
maria-g: heads-up — runtime + infra need to agree on the exact signals for KV/prefix effectiveness before the console dashboard PR lands. currently getting conflicting numbers from local dashboards :/
ajay: can you call out which numbers are diverging? hit-rate vs reuse-rate?
sarah-l: i think the main pain is 'reuse by workload' vs 'prefix reuse' definitions. one counts tenant-level reuse, the other counts prefix-level reuse, leading to double-counting in aggregated views.
maria-g: yes. example we saw: a single request can increment `kv_hits` and `prefix_reuse` if the prefix cache was used then kv cache fallback hit — that inflates 'overall effectiveness' if you sum them.
tolga: from infra side: we emit counters per backend operation (kv_hit, kv_miss, prefix_hit, prefix_evict). question is whether dashboard should compute rates from counters or ingest derived gauges from runtime. both have tradeoffs.
kevin-p: also worried about high-cardinality labels on `prefix_*` metrics (tenant_id, model, route). naive dashboarding -> OOM in grafana when expanding by model. we need sampled rollups.
ajay: proposal: canonical metric set we expose to console: `kv_total_ops`, `kv_hit_count`, `prefix_total_ops`, `prefix_reuse_count`, `prefix_evictions`. primary keys: model, route, workload_tag (low-cardinality). runtime keeps full labels but infra ships sampled rollups for console.
sarah-l: +1, but we need a precise definition doc for each metric. e.g. prefix_reuse_count = number of requests where a cached prefix was reused to satisfy at least one token generation step (not just a KV lookup).
maria-g: good. also define ordering for fallbacks: if prefix_reuse AND kv_hit both true, count only the prefix_reuse for "effective_cached_request" to avoid double-counting.
tolga: we can implement that by emitting an ordered boolean label `cache_layer_used=prefix|kv|none` from runtime and aggregate on that. cheaper than heuristics.
kevin-p: for dashboards we should provide both: 1) raw counters with cardinality labels (ingested to long-term TSDB), 2) pre-aggregated low-cardinality rollups for console. sampling plan: sample 1% of requests but biased towards heavy models and failed requests.
ajay: questions on eviction metric: do we care about eviction reason? memory_pressure vs LRU. we could expose `prefix_eviction_reason` but that's higher cardinality. maybe separate counter `prefix_evictions_memory_pressure` + `prefix_evictions_lru` (low-card).
sarah-l: UX note: console should show both hit-rate (hits / total_ops) and reuse-per-workload (unique requests that benefited). user wants to quickly see cost savings estimate. add `estimated_tokens_saved` derived gauge.
observability-bot: auto-sample-query: `SELECT sum(prefix_reuse_count)/sum(prefix_total_ops) as prefix_reuse_rate FROM metrics WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY model, workload_tag` (note: requires rollup table for stable response).
maria-g: thanks. action items: (1) runtime to add `cache_layer_used` label + fine-grained counters, (2) infra to produce low-cardinality rollups with sampling plan, (3) product/console to design dashboard widgets that avoid summing misaligned metrics. can we have owners + ETA?
tolga: infra will add rollup pipeline schema and sampling by EOD next week.
ajay: runtime will add `cache_layer_used` and the precise metric docs draft by Monday.
kevin-p: i'll prototype the rollup query and a grafana panel with sampling fallbacks by Thursday.
sarah-l: i'll mock the console widgets and the cost-savings calc, schedule review.
maria-g: perfect. scheduling 30m sync Wed 9am PT to finalize naming and queries. pinging owners in calendar invite. :thumbsup:
